records.failureSummary: DATABASE slice for TaskBoard: the runtime config module (src/config.js) and JSON persistence store (src/store.js) fully satisfy the task acceptance criteria and are verified by focused tests. DATA_DIR parsing defaults to ./data and resolves an explicit override to an absolute path (path.resolve), rejecting NUL bytes; ensureDataDir creates the directory (recursive mkdir), asserts it is a directory and R_OK|W_OK writable. JsonStore keeps a single JSON data file (db.json) strictly inside DATA_DIR, loads it on startup (empty state on ENOENT, StoreError on corrupt JSON), and persists mutations with a same-directory temp file + fsync + rename atomic write so readers never see a half-written file. Restart with the same DATA_DIR reloads persisted users/tasks; only Node stdlib (node:fs, node:path, node:crypto) is used, with zero runtime dependencies. Changes this turn: hardened JsonStore.#writeAtomic so any failure (open/write/fsync/rename) removes the temp file and leaves the previously persisted state untouched, and added a store test proving concurrent updates are serialised into one consistent data file. Verification: node --test src/tests/store.test.js src/tests/config.test.js src/tests/persistence.test.js -> 17 tests, 17 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors; node src/scripts/lint.js -> exit 0. Note: the two new end-to-end [AC-04] HTTP tests in src/tests/ac04-data-security.test.js still fail with 404 because POST /api/register is not wired into createServer; that wiring is a BACKEND task and is out of scope for this DATABASE slice (the storage layer already hashes passwords via scrypt and never persists plaintext).
